prerequisites: Application of design, analysis, and testing methods for mechanical elements, structures, and systems

learning_outcomes.text: Theoretical calculation and experimental determination of mechanical characteristics for materials containing defects
Possibility of diagnosis and expertise in Mechanical Engineering based on the knowledge acquired within this discipline
Methodologies for predicting failure risk will be acquired, combined with statistical analysis of post-factum in-service inspection
New concepts such as variability and uncertainty, associated with any expertise based on identifying the risk of component failure, will be assimilated
The influence of part size, manufacturing defects, cleavage in structural steels, fatigue, and stress corrosion cracking on fracture failure will be highlighted and clarified
Steps in fatigue design
Stages of fatigue degradation
Characteristics of the continuous variation periodic cycle
Determination of fatigue limit by plotting the Wöhler curve
Haigh type limit cycle diagram
Schematizations of the Haigh diagram
Effect of stress concentration on fatigue loads
Fatigue safety factor
Calculation of the safety factor based on the schematization of the limit cycle diagram
Respects teaching staff at lectures, seminars, and labs during didactic hours interaction
Respects disciplinary and professional instructions of teaching staff for lectures, seminars, and labs
Forms working groups based on which they work in both laboratory and seminar to solve tasks provided by the teacher
Documents himself before and after the lecture, seminar, and laboratory regarding the issues to be discussed or already discussed on-site
Will be active in lectures, seminars, and laboratory sessions
Will summarize laboratory works, pay attention in class, and perform relevant calculations
Will study during individual study hours for both laboratory and seminar sessions
Will take the two tests provided in the disciplinary calendar plan

syllabus_topics: Introductory notions
Fatigue fracture. Physical phenomenon
Characteristics of the continuous variation periodic cycle
Fatigue durability curve: Wöhler
Fatigue strength diagrams
Factors influencing fatigue fracture
Fatigue safety factor
Material fatigue in the high durability range
Calculation for variable loads with constant amplitude. Safety factor. Probability of failure
Fatigue behavior of materials under real loads
Life estimation for variable loads with constant amplitude
Fatigue crack propagation. Characteristic quantities
Mechanical properties and linear elastic behavior of materials
Real behavior of materials
Defects and stress concentrations
Characteristic quantities of Fracture Mechanics
Static and dynamic fatigue of materials containing defects

Occupational safety. Presentation of fracture modes. Presentation of testing machines in the Materials Strength laboratory. Shapes and types of specimens used for fatigue loading. Fatigue testing machines
Determination of fatigue limit by plane bending loading after an alternating-symmetric cycle
Determination of fatigue limit by tension-compression loading after an alternating cycle
Study of the influence of stress concentrators on fatigue life
Fatigue loading by torsion performed with an adapted device for universal testing machines - pulsators
Compound fatigue loading by tension-torsion
Laboratory make-up sessions
teaching_methods: Dual lecture using smart board, existing course projection, and conventional board (for calculations and problem solving)
Interactive lectures with approximately 25% student interaction
Bonus points for student answers in lectures (1-3 points for the exam grade)
Consultation with students on expertises related to current graduate concerns
Laboratory work requiring students to summarize and learn important notions from published lab work (machine operation, devices, calculation relations, working method)
Presentation of experimental results to the teacher during laboratory sessions
Discussions on practical applicability of lab work (at the start and after data processing)
On-site presence of students during laboratory sessions
Prior activation of all experimental stands and related equipment for laboratory work
assessment_rules: Conditions for promotion require a minimum grade of 5 for both laboratory and the exam. The final evaluation result is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity. Whole grades from 1 to 10 will be awarded, with grade 5 certifying the acquisition of minimum learning outcomes and the granting of corresponding study credits.
